assessments.reasoning: Lines 134–136 identify object code and executables, retain §§1 and 2, and require one of the following alternatives. The opening therefore rules out treating §3(c) as a standalone permission or the sole binary-distribution route. Bytes [6963,7173) match the frozen digest.

Lines 142–153 require the received written offer to remain valid for at least three years and cover any third party. It must offer complete machine-readable corresponding source on a customary interchange medium under §§1 and 2, at a charge capped at the physical cost of source distribution. Section 3(c) expressly connects that offer to binary receipt, noncommercial redistribution and passing on its information. Bytes [7392,8100) match the frozen digest.

challenge.method: Start with noncommercial redistribution of object code received with a compliant written offer, with its information passed on and §§1 and 2 satisfied as applicable. Change one fact at a time: make redistribution commercial, replace the received offer with a bare notice, limit it to the immediate recipient, or omit its information from the outgoing copy.
challenge.results: The baseline satisfies §3(c). Commercial redistribution fails its noncommercial condition even with the same offer. A bare notice fails the qualifying-offer condition. An immediate-recipient-only offer fails §3(b)'s requirement to serve any third party. Omitting the received information fails the accompaniment condition even when the original offer qualifies.

limitations: The conclusion concerns only the §3(c) route under version 2. Sections 3(a) and 3(b) provide separate routes. No actual distribution was assessed.
reasoning: Under GPL version 2, §3(c) allows a noncommercial redistributor who received object code or an executable with a qualifying §3(b) offer to accompany the redistributed binary with the information received about that offer. The opening of §3 retains the applicable terms of §§1 and 2.
